summary: Minister of Public Works Juan Edghill's first recorded response to the resignation demands. He declines to engage the substance, saying he will speak "at the appropriate time", and of the protests: "My life is in God's hands and that's not today." Five opposition parties now demand the removal of both Edghill and Minister Indar. Prime Minister Phillips defends both remaining in office and calls the opposition's parliamentary protest "irresponsible, reckless, childish, immature".

A social media post by a Guyanese news account reporting that members and supporters of the Amerindian Peoples Association staged a peaceful picket outside the Office of the President on 29 July, demanding accountability for the disaster and the removal of Ministers Edghill and Indar. When filed this was the only record of the picket held here and the archive noted that no press report of it appeared in the corpus. That note was withdrawn on 30 July: Kaieteur News, News Room, Kiskadee Watch and Demerara Waves all carry the picket. The post is retained as the earliest record of it held here.

A second, independent social media account of the same 29 July picket outside the Office of the President, reporting that many Guyanese joined it to demand accountability and justice. It gives the death figure as "about 100 people", a round number rather than an official toll.
